thread.title: UPDATE: As Apple announces new Austin campus, here's a look at the biggest hiring announcements of the year

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: As Apple announces new Austin campus, here's a look at the biggest hiring announcements of the year
text:
By Steve Goldstein, MarketWatch
Apple on Thursday announced it was building an Austin, Texas, campus, one of many hiring announcements made by companies across the nation.
Apple (AAPL) had in January announced plans to hire 20,000 workers, so the Texas campus plan (http://www.marketwatch.com/press-release/apple-to-build-new-campus-in-austin-and-add-jobs-across-the-us-2018-12-13) is not actually a new hiring announcement.
Per outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas, here are the largest hiring announcements of 2018, excluding the seasonal job hiring from the likes of Target and UPS.
Amazon (AMZN) is not number-one on the list because the initial HQ2 hiring plan of 50,000 was announced in September 2017. But the Nashville operations center the company unveiled in October puts the Jeff Bezos-run company on the list for 2018.
Andrew Challenger, vice president for Challenger, Gray & Christmas, said the big job announcements tend to be either from technology giants making strategic shifts or retailers making a big seasonal push.
Company Hires Apple US:AAPL 20,000 Starbucks US:SBUX 8,500 Dollar General US:DG 7,000 Wawa 5,000 Amazon (Nashville) US:AMZN 5,000 JP Morgan Chase US:JPM 4,000 Universal Orlando 3,000 Infosys US:INFY 3,000 Fiat Chrysler Automobiles US:FCAU 2,500 Fidelity Bank 2,500 UPS US:UPS (Atlanta) 2,500 Amazon (Boston) 2,000 Exelon US:EXC 1,800 UPS (Utah) 1,700 Darien Lake 1,600 Regeneron US:REGN 1,500 Zulily 1,200 Robins Air Force Base 1,200 Micron Technology US:MU 1,100 Cognizant US:CTSH 1,100 JSW Steel 1,000 Amazon (Michigan) 1,000 Publix 1,000 Vets First Choice 1,000 Aldi 1,000 Wayfair US:W 1,000 Salesforce US:CRM 1,000 Merit Medical Systems US:MMSI 1,000 Choctaw Casino OK 1,000
On the seasonal side, Target (TGT) announced it was hiring 120,000 workers, UPS and Amazon each said they were hiring 100,000, Kohl's (KSS) said it was hiring 90,000 workers and Home Depot (HD) and Macy's (M) said they were hiring 80,000 workers.
"These are as large as we're ever tracked," said Challenger of the temporary retail hiring. He points out that the retail demand for labor comes with unemployment at a 49-year low (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-adds-155000-jobs-in-november-unemployment-flat-at-37-2018-12-07) and consumer confidence (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/consumer-sentiment-index-holds-near-highs-in-december-2018-12-07) around post-recession highs.
-Steve Goldstein;
